tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

content.text:
I traced the whole connect flow in the code. It's on `main` and looks correct, so the cause is almost certainly the deployment's config, not a code bug. I can't see your Vercel logs or your production Supabase from here, so this is a list of likely causes, ordered by how well each one fits "connected, but nothing shows":

**How the flow works.** Moneo only shows banks connected through its own **Import → Connected banks → Connect bank** button. Clicking it creates a `pending` row. The bank then sends you to `/api/bank/callback`, which marks the row `active`. The list only shows `active`, `expired` and `error` rows ([connections/route.ts](app/api/bank/connections/route.ts)). A row stuck at `pending` is invisible, and so is a connection that never went through this button.

**Likely causes:**

1. **You only linked accounts in the Enable Banking control panel.** That step (README step 4) just allows those accounts. Moneo doesn't know about them until you also click **Connect bank** inside Moneo.
2. **`NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` isn't set in Vercel, or points to a different domain than the one you use.** The callback URL is built from it, and it defaults to `http://localhost:3000` ([env.ts:9](lib/env.ts:9)). If the bank sends you back to another domain, you aren't logged in there. The callback then sends you to `/login` and the row stays `pending`, which is invisible. `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are fixed when the app is built, so after adding or changing one you have to **redeploy**.
3. **The bank migrations were never applied to production Supabase.** A Vercel deploy doesn't run `supabase/migrations/`. You need to run `202610160101_bank_connections.sql` and `202610160102_reset_workspace_bank_connections.sql` yourself. If the tables are missing, Connect fails with "The bank connection could not be started".
4. **The redirect URL in the Enable Banking app doesn't exactly match** `https://<your-domain>/api/bank/callback`.
5. **Missing secrets:** `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Without them you'd see "Bank sync is not configured", or the connection would show as an error.

**The quickest way to tell these apart:** after you approve at the bank, look at the URL you land on.
- `/import?bank=connected`: the connection worked, but the list didn't load. Check the network response for `/api/bank/connections`.
- `?bank=invalid`: the state was lost (cause 2) or the link was over an hour old.
- `?bank=error`: creating the session failed. The row should show the error.
- `/login`, or a different domain: cause 2.

You can also run `select status, last_error, created_at from bank_connections order by created_at desc;` in the Supabase SQL editor. No rows means cause 1 or 3. A `pending` row means cause 2.

Send me your production URL and what you land on after the bank redirect, and I'll narrow it down.

**Migrations:** every migration is applied, so I didn't need to apply anything. I compared all 71 files in `supabase/migrations/` against Supabase's tracking table (`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`) on your production database. The database at `fcqjjwxpywjkbiejngbv` is the one your `.env` points to. Every file is recorded as applied, including `202610160101_bank_connections` and `202610160102_reset_workspace_bank_connections`. The `bank_connections` table exists with the expected columns.

The database also lists one migration the repo doesn't have, `202610080019 conversation_context`. It was probably applied from another branch, and it doesn't affect banking.

There are **0 rows** in `bank_connections`, so Moneo has never completed a connection. That fits what you're seeing: the "not configured" message hides the Connect button, so the flow never starts.

**Why it says "not configured":** I can't see your Vercel settings, but this message appears when the deployment can't read one of these three variables ([enable-banking.ts:67-76](lib/bank/enable-banking.ts:67)):

- `ENABLE_BANKING_APP_ID`
- `ENABLE_BANKING_PRIVATE_KEY`
- `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`

All three must be set and non-empty. It also fails if `ENABLE_BANKING_API_URL` is set but empty or not a valid URL: leave it out entirely or set it to `https://api.enablebanking.com`. In Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables, check:

1. All three are present with the exact names above. `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is the one people most often forget. Your local `.env` has a value for it that you can copy.
2. They're enabled for the **Production** environment, not only Preview or Development.
3. `ENABLE_BANKING_API_URL` isn't set to an empty value.
4. You **redeployed after adding them**. Vercel only gives new variables to new deployments: Deployments → ⋯ → Redeploy.

Setting the redirect URL only on the Vercel (production) app is correct. Once the message is gone, the **Choose a bank → Connect bank** button will appear.

content.text:
I found the cause and it's a missing Vercel setting, not a code bug, so I didn't change any code. I didn't need your browser: I tested your Enable Banking app directly from here.

**What's wrong:** the app builds the bank's return address from `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`. That variable isn't set in Vercel, so the app uses its fallback, `http://localhost:3000` ([env.ts:9](lib/env.ts:9)). Enable Banking only accepts the return address you registered, so it rejects every start request. The app shows that rejection as "The bank connection could not be started".

I sent the same start request to Enable Banking with each return address:

| Return address | Enable Banking's answer |
| --- | --- |
| `http://localhost:3000/api/bank/callback` | 400 "Redirect URI not allowed" |
| `https://moneo-mu.vercel.app/api/bank/callback` | 200, sends back the bank login link |

Your Enable Banking app itself is fine: it's in Production, active, and its only registered return address is `https://moneo-mu.vercel.app/api/bank/callback`.

**To fix it in Vercel:**
1. Settings → Environment Variables → add `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` = `https://moneo-mu.vercel.app` (no trailing slash), enabled for **Production**.
2. Redeploy. This one matters more than usual: `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values are fixed when the app is built, so the setting does nothing until a new build.
3. Open the app at **moneo-mu.vercel.app**, not a `moneo-xxxx-indkhans-projects.vercel.app` deployment link. If you start on a different domain, you won't be logged in when the bank sends you back, and the connection won't finish.

Then choose a country and bank again, and it should send you to the bank's login page.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
entries.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_network_requests
entries.description: Read HTTP network requests (XHR, Fetch, documents, images, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging API calls, monitoring network activity, or understanding what requests a page is making. Returns all network requests made by the current page, including cross-origin requests. Requests are automatically cleared when the page navigates to a different domain. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read network requests from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

urlPattern.description: Optional URL pattern to filter requests. Only requests whose URL as listed (auth values shown as REDACTED) contains this string will be returned (e.g., '/api/' to filter API calls, 'example.com' to filter by domain).

clear.description: If true, clear the network requests after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

limit.description: Maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
entries.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one.

repository.description: With target "cloud", only when the user named a repository other than this project's: "owner/name" on github.com, which the cloud session clones at its default branch. Take the exact owner/name from the user's words or a listing that shows it; if you are not sure of it, ask them. A bypass or auto permission mode may not carry over: the session then starts in the cloud's default mode. If the call is refused, do not run or propose the other repository's work in this project.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

input.title: Fix bank sync never advancing last_booked_on
input.prompt: Investigate and fix why bank sync never records progress in production. In workflows/bank-sync.ts, finishBankSync should set bank_connection_accounts.last_booked_on once an import is completed, and set bank_connections.last_synced_at. Production data (Supabase, SUPABASE_DB_URL in .env; read with a small node script using node_modules/postgres) shows: connection a1376c53-8788-432b-aaab-b4bc3ad692e1 has one account whose last_booked_on is still NULL after two completed sync imports (8b71096b… at 2026-10-16T21:03 and 233d5006… at 21:19, both status completed). last_synced_at = 21:04:31 covers only the first sync; the second sync never updated it. So every sync re-fetches the full 90-day window and adds a full-size import-history entry. Find the root cause: check how syncBankConnection calls importFile (a nested "use workflow" function) from a workflow under Vercel Workflow, whether finishBankSync's status read/update can silently do nothing, and check workflows/bank-sync.test.ts. Read node_modules/next/dist/docs and the workflow package docs as needed. Done = a root-cause fix plus a test that fails without it, with npm test and npm run lint passing, committed on a branch, and a PR opened against main.
input.background: Moneo (Next.js 16, Supabase, Vercel Workflow) syncs Revolut through Enable Banking. Each sync is written as an ordinary CSV import, so dedupe on the bank transaction id, review and undo work as for any import. The data itself is correct: 131 transactions and a €136.72 balance snapshot. The bug is only that sync progress is never recorded. Follow AGENTS.md: keep changes scoped, no rewrites of applied migrations, and commit each logical piece.

# Database regression checks

Run `node supabase/tests/run-recurring-occurrences.mjs` for migration `202610060003` and its explicit occurrence fixture on the configured database. It checks current-owner/version/date guards, partial/full and pending-to-posted receipts, undo/reassociation/deletion history and authenticated isolation. Candidate schema and migration history are verified unchanged after rollback.

Run `node supabase/tests/recurring-occurrence-concurrency.mjs` to check association versus transaction correction on separate authenticated connections. It creates only a disposable application schema with synthetic users, verifies correction/association lock order and stale-version rejection, then drops that exact schema and verifies cleanup. Public migration history and schema privileges remain unchanged; an ignored `.qa` recovery journal records the disposable schema if interrupted.

Run `node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs` with the existing `.env` configuration. The script verifies that `SUPABASE_DB_URL` targets `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, then tests pending migrations against the deployed application schema and replays every migration into a temporary isolated schema. It compares columns, constraints, indexes, RLS, policies, views, triggers and application functions, and runs the synthetic `.sql` regressions on both paths.

All writes run inside rollback-only transactions. Migration history stays unchanged, and the script verifies that its temporary schema was removed. It does not apply migrations permanently. Fresh verification uses an empty `auth.users` surrogate and skips Supabase-owned storage bucket/policy setup; full Supabase platform bootstrap still requires a disposable local Supabase instance.

`workspace-isolation.sql` seeds two synthetic users and foreign records in every current application table. It switches to the actual `authenticated` database role to check row visibility and foreign-target RPC denial. Keep its fixture list and RPC cases aligned when adding tables or mutations.

Run `node supabase/tests/precision.mjs` to verify the actual Money/budget page SELECTs through PostgREST with amounts beyond JavaScript's safe integer range. This check temporarily commits a synthetic user/workspace and removes only those records in `finally`; it verifies cleanup. It requires the existing service-role key, which is never printed.

Run `node supabase/tests/chat-concurrency.mjs` after migration 023 is applied to check duplicate claims and cancellation on separate authenticated connections. It verifies cancellation waits for the execution lock and prevents later corrections/replies, then removes its synthetic user/workspace.

Run `node supabase/tests/review-concurrency.mjs` after migration 043 is applied to exercise review finish/cancel and first preference-insert races on separate real authenticated/service connections. Cancellation or scope revocation prevents analysis persistence; a committed finisher retains its historical result. Synthetic fixtures are removed by exact IDs.

Run `node supabase/tests/import-concurrency.mjs` after migration 051 is applied to check cancellation and ingestion on separate authenticated/service connections. It observes the specific waiter and holder database process locks, verifies cancellation cannot admit later row effects, retains already committed source evidence, fences old workers after resume and deduplicates simultaneous retries. Its exact large-money synthetic records are removed by ID.

Run `node supabase/tests/summary-live.mjs` with the local app running and its existing `CRON_SECRET` configured to verify actual cron dispatch, free-model review completion, period deduplication, cancellation and disabling. It uses a disposable empty workspace and targeted cleanup. This verifies the local endpoint/workflow; it does not prove that Vercel's external daily cron has been deployed.

Run `npx playwright test e2e/two-user-isolation.gated.spec.ts --reporter=list` for two real disposable authenticated users. It exercises page/API/file ownership, denied foreign review cancellation, account editing/archive/sequential undo, saved view rename/removal/filter replacement/undo, Home insight dismissal/restore, exact large relevance thresholds and type mute/unmute. It requires the configured admin/auth/database environment, sends no email, uses no saved credentials or mocked backend, and removes its fixtures. Recovery IDs are written to ignored `.qa` files only if interrupted.

`insight-preferences.sql` checks owner isolation, exact thresholds beyond JavaScript's safe integer range, dismissal deduplication, bounded lookahead and dismissal restoration. The pure insight fixtures cover all nine supported types, dated evidence changes, ambiguity suppression, half-up medians and filling the item limit after dismissed evidence is removed. Insights make no model calls.

For the targeted import review regression only, use `node supabase/tests/run-sql.mjs --candidate` before applying migration 020, or omit `--candidate` afterward. It also rolls back its synthetic fixtures and candidate function replacement.

Run `node supabase/tests/run-goal-reservations.mjs` for the reservation boundary/history fixture. For SQL/application resolver parity, run `RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS=1 npm test -- lib/finance/reservation-balance.live.test.ts` (PowerShell: set `$env:RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS='1'` first). This opt-in test compares six synthetic balance fixtures and rolls everything back.

import sys
S=sys.argv[1]
old="""      select ts.transaction_id from public.transaction_sources ts
      where ts.transaction_id = any (txn_ids)
      group by ts.transaction_id having count(*) > 1"""
new="""      select ts.transaction_id from public.transaction_sources ts
      join public.source_transactions st on st.id = ts.source_transaction_id
      left join public.imports i on i.id = st.import_id
      where ts.transaction_id = any (txn_ids) and i.status is distinct from 'undone'
      group by ts.transaction_id having count(*) > 1"""
out=[]
for f in ("preview.sql","undo.sql"):
    d=open(f"{S}/{f}",encoding="utf8").read().replace("\r\n","\n").strip()
    assert d.count(old)==1, f
    d=d.replace(old,new)
    if f=="undo.sql":
        anchor="""  delete from public.balance_snapshots
  where workspace_id = import_row.workspace_id
    and provenance like 'import:' || p_import_id::text || ':%';
"""
        assert d.count(anchor)==1
        d=d.replace(anchor, anchor+"""
  -- Matched links kept by an already-undone duplicate import no longer hold these transactions.
  delete from public.transaction_sources ts
  using public.source_transactions st, public.imports i
  where ts.source_transaction_id = st.id and i.id = st.import_id
    and i.status = 'undone' and ts.transaction_id = any (txn_ids);
""")
    out.append(d+";\n")

-- re-import (e.g. a repeated bank sync) left the original import permanently un-undoable.
-- Same bodies as the live definitions plus the undone-import filter and stale-link cleanup.

"""
open("supabase/migrations/202610170001_undo_ignores_undone_matches.sql","w",encoding="utf8",newline="\n").write(head+"\n".join(out))
EOF

OPEN  2026-10-11T15:46:04Z by Kikeskr
## Environment
- OS: Windows
- Entire CLI: 0.11.4
- Integration: Codex desktop
- Repository: public project repo (SignalForge)

## Expected
Following the documented checkpoint workflow, a normal Git commit after the Entire session becomes idle should have `prepare-commit-msg` add the checkpoint trailer and `post-commit` finalize/condense the checkpoint.

## Observed
- Entire hook approvals are present; repository status shows enabled and sync target `origin`.

- The stalled processes were stopped; hooks were not bypassed and no changes were reset/discarded.
- `git ls-remote https://github.com/Kikeskr/SignalForge.git` succeeds. Proxy environment variables and Git proxy settings were absent; WinHTTP reports direct access.
- An earlier Entire log had a GitHub checkpoint-ref enumeration failure via `127.0.0.1:443`, but the latest stall is not established to be network-related.
- `entire status --json`: enabled, sync target `origin`, session idle/active state changes between runs; no pending approvals.

=== #2725
CLOSED COMPLETED 2026-10-10T23:25:59Z by Haikeysgit
**Version:** Entire CLI 0.11.4 (go1.27.1), entire_windows_amd64.zip from the v0.11.4 release
**OS:** Windows 11 Pro 22621, Git for Windows (bash), commits made from Claude Code (desktop app)

**Repro**
1. `entire enable --agent claude-code` in a repo (hooks installed: prepare-commit-msg, commit-msg, post-commit, post-rewrite, pre-push).
2. Start a Claude Code session in that repo. `entire session list` shows it as active (long session, ~33M tokens).
3. Stage a one-file docs change and run `git commit -m "..."`.

**Expected:** commit completes, with an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
**Actual:** `git commit` never returns. Killed after 9 minutes (`timeout 540`). Running the hook directly hangs the same way:
`timeout 20 entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <msgfile> message` → exit 124.

**Notes**
- `entire doctor`: all checks OK, "No stuck sessions found".
- A commit made in the same clone *before* the session was being captured completed instantly (no trailer, `No sessions`).
- `git commit --no-verify` still hangs (prepare-commit-msg isn't skipped by --no-verify). Workaround: `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit`.
- Possibly related to transcript size: the active session is very large.

content.text:
Both fixes are pushed to `main` in three commits and live on Vercel.

**1. Only 14 of 131 transactions came back.** Leaving the page wasn't the cause: the sync runs on the server whether or not you're watching. The real cause was the sync's "start from" date. Each sync only re-fetches from a week before the last date it recorded, which was Oct 16. When you undid the imports, that date stayed, so the next sync only asked Revolut for Oct 9–16 (14 transactions).
- `f63e5b2`: undoing an import now clears that account's start date, so the next sync fetches the full 90 days again. Transactions you still have are matched by their bank IDs, not added twice.
- I also cleared the date for your Revolut account now, so your next sync fetches all 90 days without you needing to undo anything first. That's why the account currently shows "not synced yet".

**2. No way to see what a sync is doing.**
- `b2e54b4`: the sync records when it started, so its state is stored on the server. That lets it show up even after you leave the page and come back. Clicking "Sync now" while a sync is already running is refused.
- `a9b82ef`: while a sync runs, the bank card shows a live panel with an elapsed-time counter and three steps:
  1. Asking Revolut for transactions and balance

content.text:
Moneo now asks for everything, but Revolut decides how much it shares, and right now that's about 90 days.

**What I tested:** I asked Revolut for all transactions on your account since 2015. It returned the same **131 transactions, from Jul 21 to Oct 16**. So the 90 days in the code wasn't what limited you: Revolut sends about 90 days no matter how far back you ask.

**Why:** under the EU open-banking rules (PSD2), banks usually share only about the last 90 days once some time has passed since you approved access. Many share older history only in a short window right after you approve. Your consent dates from yesterday, so that window has passed. Your account could also simply have no transactions before Jul 21; you'd know that better than me.

**What I changed** (`74d8141`, pushed to `main`): when an account has no sync start date, the sync now asks for everything since 2000 instead of 90 days. That covers the first sync after connecting, which runs right after approval when banks share the most, and the next sync after you undo a sync import. Banks that reject such an old start date get the 90-day request instead. I added a test for both paths, updated the README, and the full test suite and lint pass.

**To get older history:** disconnect Revolut in Moneo and connect it again. The first sync runs right after you approve, which is the best chance of getting older data. I haven't tested whether Revolut actually sends more in that case. Your existing transactions would be matched by their bank IDs, so nothing gets duplicated.

One known limit: a single account with more than 10,000 transactions makes the sync stop with an error. That's an existing safety cap, and a very long full history could hit it.
